original.target_description: Teen-reported friendship quality (FQS); Treatment versus Delayed Treatment Control, baseline-to-post-treatment Condition X Time ANOVA, adolescents with ASD.

n.quote: Thirty-three teens between 13 and 17 years of age with ASD participated in and completed this study with their parents.
n.sample_role: Adolescent participants: treatment n = 17; delayed-treatment control n = 16; analytic sample for target ANOVA.
n.exclusions: Three additional participants dropped out: one never started, one left after anxiety at first session, one discontinued for missing more than three sessions. Pilot groups excluded.

es.location: p. 602, Results, Condition X Time interaction

p.location: p. 602, Results, Condition X Time interaction

replication.target_description: Friendship quality (FQS); experimental treatment versus waitlist control, pre-to-post Group X Time interaction, adolescents with ASD.

n.location: PDF p. 6, Figure 1 CONSORT; PDF p. 11, Table 3 group header
n.sample_role: Adolescent participants: experimental n = 29; waitlist control n = 29; analytic parent/adolescent sample.
n.exclusions: Of 71 assessed, 8 excluded (2 did not attend intake; 6 failed IQ criterion); 63 randomized, 5 experimental participants discontinued; 29 per group analyzed. Missing items multiply imputed (<10.34% per scale). QSQ outliers winsorized, not deleted.

es.location: PDF p. 11, Table 3, Friendship quality (FQS) row; table note: interaction p value

p.location: PDF p. 11, Table 3, Friendship quality (FQS) row; table note: interaction p value

reported_success.quote: In contrast to the original PEERS study, the current study did not find that friendship quality significantly improved in the experimental treatment group.

notes: Original F statistic retained as printed; no effect-size conversion. Replication refers to final analyzed sample. Replication Table 3 prints ns for the target interaction; no numeric p, interaction statistic, or standardized effect size is printed for that outcome. ns retained in the quote; numerical p and bound are null. Original interaction reflects deterioration in controls; original treatment within-group FQS improvement was not significant.
